title: Throughput-optimized many-core over few complex cores
decision: Design eight simple in-order cores on a single die instead of fewer large out-of-order cores, optimizing for aggregate throughput
alternatives_or_rejected: The industry trend of building fewer, wider, more aggressively speculative out-of-order cores targeting high single-thread performance
rationale: Commercial server workloads exhibit abundant thread-level parallelism but poor instruction-level parallelism and are memory-latency-bound; many simple cores deliver higher aggregate throughput and better power efficiency for these workloads
outcome: 32 threads on one die with significantly higher throughput on commercial benchmarks than contemporary high-frequency single-thread processors, at the cost of lower single-thread performance

title: Fine-grained multithreading with four threads per core
decision: Implement fine-grained multithreading with four hardware threads per core, switching threads on a cycle-by-cycle basis
alternatives_or_rejected: Coarse-grained multithreading, simultaneous multithreading on a wide out-of-order core, or single-threaded in-order cores
rationale: Fine-grained switching hides cache miss and memory latency effectively without requiring complex out-of-order execution hardware; with four threads, the simple in-order pipeline can almost always find a ready instruction to execute
outcome: High pipeline utilization and effective latency tolerance on memory-bound workloads, enabling the use of a simple in-order core

title: In-order execution pipeline
decision: Use a simple in-order execution pipeline rather than an out-of-order superscalar design
alternatives_or_rejected: Out-of-order execution with register renaming, dynamic scheduling, and speculative execution
rationale: Out-of-order logic consumes substantial die area and power for issue queues, rename registers, and bypass networks; for memory-bound commercial workloads, multithreading hides latency more efficiently than out-of-order speculation, and the area savings enable more cores
outcome: Small, power-efficient cores that fit eight instances on the die, with aggregate throughput exceeding complex OOO designs on target workloads

title: Single shared floating-point unit
decision: Provide only one floating-point unit shared among all eight cores, rather than one per core
alternatives_or_rejected: A dedicated floating-point unit in each core, or no FPU at all
rationale: Commercial server workloads are overwhelmingly integer-dominated, making per-core FPUs an inefficient use of die area; a single shared FPU provides adequate throughput for the rare FP operations while saving substantial area for additional integer cores and caches
outcome: Sufficient floating-point performance for target workloads with major die area savings, though FP-intensive codes perform poorly

title: On-chip memory controllers with crossbar interconnect
decision: Integrate memory controllers on-chip and connect cores to multiple L2 cache banks via a non-blocking crossbar
alternatives_or_rejected: Off-chip memory controllers accessed via a front-side bus, or a shared bus connecting cores to memory
rationale: 32 concurrent threads generate enormous memory bandwidth demand that would saturate an off-chip or shared-bus solution; on-chip controllers reduce latency and the crossbar provides non-blocking concurrent access to independent L2 banks and memory channels
outcome: Sustained memory bandwidth matching the throughput of 32 threads, without the bottlenecks of traditional front-side bus architectures
